topic: Real Numbers, Intervals, Absolute Value & Inequalities
core_points: Real number system hierarchy: N ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R
Axiomatic properties: Algebraic, Order, and the Completeness Property
Finite and infinite intervals in set, interval, and graphical notations
Geometric and algebraic piecewise definitions of |x|
Linear inequality mechanics and negative sign reversal

deep_dive.content: Unlike the set of rational numbers Q, which contains infinitely many 'holes' (like √2 or π), the real line R is complete. Formally, every non-empty subset of R bounded above has a least upper bound (supremum). This property is foundational because limits and continuity cannot exist without it.

Rather than thinking of |x| merely as 'making a number positive', view it as the metric distance between two points. The inequality |x - c| < δ describes an open symmetric interval (c - δ, c + δ) centered at c with radius δ. This notation is the backbone for the formal (ε, δ) definition of limits coming up in Week 3.

Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number inverts the order relation. Geometrically, multiplying by -1 reflects the coordinate point across the origin, swapping the directional hierarchy on the real axis.
